name: Listen to calming music you choose
min_effective_dose: Single listening session (minutes not stated in the meta-analysis abstract; ~20-30 min unconfirmed)
instruction: Put on music you find relaxing and simply listen for a while. Choosing the tracks yourself and listening in order to relax is what the evidence supports.

name: Stay on sad music
instruction: Not suggested on its own. If music is chosen while sad, start with a track that matches the mood and move toward a brighter one over two or three tracks.
contraindicated_for: sad=Self-selected sad music increased depressed mood in people prone to rumination (Garrido & Schubert 2015; not in PubMed);;condition:rumination_prone=Same finding

name: Listen to upbeat music
instruction: Play a few upbeat songs you like. People report this helps raise energy, but the evidence is a self-report survey only.
contraindicated_for: angry=Arousal-increasing activities do not reduce anger (Kjaervik & Bushman 2024);;context:near_bedtime=Activating

name: Dance freely to a song
min_effective_dose: 5 min single session (Campion & Levita 2014, via Koch 2019 full text; single small study)
instruction: Put on a song and move however you like for about five minutes, in private, with nobody watching or judging.
contraindicated_for: angry=Arousal-increasing activity; not shown to reduce anger

name: Join a dance class or dance regularly
instruction: Plan a regular dance class or session. The evidence is for multi-week group programmes, not a single dance.
contraindicated_for: context:quick_mood_lift_needed=Evidence is programme-level (mean 11.4 weeks)

name: Draw something you can see
min_effective_dose: Single short session after a mood induction (minutes not checkable)
instruction: Pick an object nearby and draw it for about ten minutes. Focus on the object, not on how you feel.

name: Draw something that makes you happy
min_effective_dose: Single session (minutes not checkable)
instruction: Draw something that makes you happy for about ten minutes. Skill does not matter.

name: Draw to vent your feelings
instruction: Not suggested: drawing to vent gave no mood benefit over a control task and did worse than distracting or positive drawing.
contraindicated_for: sad=No benefit vs control (Dalebroux et al. 2008; not in PubMed);;angry=Expressing did worse than distracting (Genuth & Drake 2021; not in PubMed);;context:quick_mood_lift_needed=Null for acute mood repair

name: Colour a mandala or patterned design
min_effective_dose: Single session (~20 min, unverified)
requirements: colouring page and pens (or a colouring app)
instruction: Choose a mandala or patterned design you like and colour it for about twenty minutes. A structured design works better than a blank page.

name: Shape clay or modelling dough
min_effective_dose: Single short session after a mood induction; 30 min in one small study
instruction: Knead and shape a piece of clay or modelling dough for a while, making anything you like.

name: Play an instrument you already play
min_effective_dose: 30 min (single small study; not checkable in PubMed)
instruction: Play an instrument you already know for around half an hour, just for yourself with no audience.

name: Sing with no audience
min_effective_dose: One low-pressure session (15 professional singers)
instruction: Sing along to something you like, on your own and with no one listening or judging.
contraindicated_for: context:performance_pressure=Cortisol rose when singing for an audience (Fancourt et al. 2015)

name: Sing with a group or choir
min_effective_dose: Single one-hour choir session (uncontrolled, special population)
instruction: Plan to join a choir or group sing. This is a plan-ahead suggestion, not something to do right now.
contraindicated_for: condition:social_anxiety=Group activity;;context:quick_mood_lift_needed=Needs a group; not right-now

name: Make free art (collage, markers, paint)
min_effective_dose: 45 min (uncontrolled study, 39 adults)
instruction: Spend up to 45 minutes making anything you like with collage, markers, paint or clay. There is no right result.

name: Therapist-led art therapy
instruction: Reference only: evidence is for multi-session therapist-led art therapy, not a self-guided activity.

name: Arts engagement (any)
instruction: Reference only: scoping-review evidence that arts engagement relates to wellbeing; no effect sizes.

name: Expressive writing about a difficult experience
instruction: Over three or four days, write for 15-20 minutes about your deepest thoughts and feelings on something difficult. Expect to feel a bit worse right afterwards; any benefit is small and shows up weeks later.
contraindicated_for: context:quick_mood_lift_needed=Short-term distress goes up and positive mood down right after writing (Baikie & Wilhelm 2005);;context:high_intensity=Do not offer to someone highly distressed with no follow-up;;sad=No significant long-term effect on depressive symptoms in healthy adults (Reinhold et al. 2018; not in PubMed)

name: Write about your best possible self
min_effective_dose: Single 20-min session in several included studies (Carrillo et al. 2019, Table 1)
instruction: Imagine a future in which everything has gone as well as it could, and write about it for up to twenty minutes.

name: Journal for a few minutes
instruction: Write for about fifteen minutes about what is on your mind, including anything that went well. The evidence is for journaling repeated over weeks, so treat one session as a start.
contraindicated_for: context:quick_mood_lift_needed=Evidence is multi-week; small effects

name: Read or write a poem
instruction: Read a poem you like, or write a few lines of your own. Evidence is preliminary and from group programmes.

name: Knit or crochet
instruction: If you already knit or crochet, pick it up for a while. Evidence comes from a survey of existing knitters.

name: Cook or bake something
instruction: Cook or bake something simple you enjoy. The evidence is for group cooking classes, so cooking with or for someone is closest to what was studied.

name: Eat a meal with someone
instruction: Arrange to eat a meal with someone. Evidence is a cross-sectional survey of habitual social eating.

name: Take a photo of something that makes you (or someone else) happy
min_effective_dose: 1 photo/day; effect seen after 3 weeks
instruction: Take one photo of something that makes you smile, or one you think would make someone else happy and send it to them.

name: Do a small creative project
instruction: Spend some time on any creative hobby you enjoy. This suits a good or energetic mood especially well.

name: Read fiction
instruction: Read a story for a while as a break. Do not expect an instant mood lift: benefit showed up only after recalling or discussing what was read.
contraindicated_for: context:quick_mood_lift_needed=No immediate effect of a single reading exposure (Carney & Robertson 2022)

name: Work through a self-help book
instruction: Plan-ahead only: structured CBT-style self-help books over weeks reduced depressive symptoms in adults with depression.
contraindicated_for: context:quick_mood_lift_needed=Weeks-long, clinical evidence

name: Self-paced moderate exercise
min_effective_dose: Single bout; fatigue falls only if >20 min low-to-moderate (Loy et al. 2013; not re-confirmed); most single-bout studies 21-40 min
instruction: Do 20-40 minutes of any movement you like at a comfortable, self-chosen pace: cycling, swimming, a fast walk. Stop if you get chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.
contraindicated_for: angry=Arousal-increasing activities did not reduce anger, g = -0.02 (Kjaervik & Bushman 2024);;context:near_bedtime=Keep it moderate in the last hour before bed

name: Go for a jog or run
instruction: Jog at an easy, self-chosen pace. The low-mood evidence is for regular jogging or walking over weeks.
contraindicated_for: angry=Do not suggest running for anger: arousal-increasing activities g = -0.02 (Kjaervik & Bushman 2024);;tired=High effort;;context:near_bedtime=Vigorous exercise ending within 1 h of bed may impair sleep

name: Take a brisk 10-minute walk
min_effective_dose: 10 min (Thayer 1987, n = 18; energy up and tension down for up to 2 h)
instruction: Walk briskly for ten minutes, outdoors if you can. In one small study this raised energy and lowered tension for up to two hours.

name: Walk the stairs for 10 minutes
min_effective_dose: 10 min low-to-moderate (18 college women; transient)
instruction: Walk up and down stairs at an easy-to-moderate pace for ten minutes.
contraindicated_for: angry=Arousal-increasing

name: Take 5-minute movement breaks each hour
min_effective_dose: 6 x 5 min moderate walking across a 6-h day (benefit seen at end of day, not after one break)
instruction: Get up and walk for five minutes now, and repeat roughly every hour for the rest of your sitting day.

name: High-intensity interval training
requirements: regular exerciser; no heart, metabolic or kidney disease
instruction: Only for people who already exercise regularly: a short interval workout. Evidence is for programmes, and hard intervals feel unpleasant while you do them.
contraindicated_for: angry=Arousal-increasing;;tired=High effort;;condition:inactive_or_cardiometabolic_disease=Medical caution for inactive users or heart/metabolic/renal disease;;context:near_bedtime=Not within 1 h of bed;;context:high_intensity=Above-threshold exercise feels worse, which matters when already distressed

name: Very hard exercise (above your comfortable pace)
instruction: Not suggested as a mood fix: above the ventilatory threshold exercise reliably feels unpleasant. Prefer a self-selected comfortable pace.
contraindicated_for: angry=Arousal-increasing activities do not reduce anger;;tired=High effort;;context:near_bedtime=Vigorous exercise ending within 1 h of bed may impair sleep (Stutz et al. 2019);;condition:inactive_or_cardiometabolic_disease=Screening advised

name: Strength training
instruction: Do a strength session with good technique. The anxiety and low-mood evidence is for regular training over weeks.
contraindicated_for: tired=High effort;;context:quick_mood_lift_needed=Programme-level evidence

name: Gentle yoga
min_effective_dose: One session (single-session meta-analysis not found in PubMed; unconfirmed)
instruction: Do a gentle, slow yoga sequence. Slower meditative styles calm more in the moment than power styles.

name: Tai chi
instruction: Practise tai chi regularly. The evidence is for regular practice over weeks to months, not one session.
contraindicated_for: context:quick_mood_lift_needed=Programme-level evidence; no acute anxiety effect confirmed

name: Qigong
instruction: Practise qigong regularly. Evidence is from a few flawed trials of 1-3 months of practice.
contraindicated_for: context:quick_mood_lift_needed=Programme-level evidence

name: 10 minutes of stretching
min_effective_dose: 10 min after work, repeated over 3 months (no single-session evidence)
instruction: Stretch gently through your neck, shoulders, back and legs for ten minutes.

name: Walk in a green space
min_effective_dose: Short engagements give benefits ("first 5 min" not in abstract); rumination evidence only at 90 min
instruction: Walk at an easy pace in a park or other green space. Even a short walk is associated with better mood; the rumination study used 90 minutes.

name: Take an awe walk
min_effective_dose: 15 min weekly for 8 weeks (older adults only)
instruction: Walk for fifteen minutes somewhere new or wide-open and look for things that feel vast or surprising, as if seeing them for the first time.

name: Spend slow time among trees
min_effective_dose: Short forest visits
instruction: If you can reach a wood or forest, walk or sit there slowly and take in the sights, sounds and smells.

name: Visit water (river, lake, sea)
instruction: Spend some time beside a river, lake or the sea. Evidence is mostly cross-sectional. Take care near water.

name: Do some gardening
min_effective_dose: 30 min after a stressor (30 experienced allotment gardeners)
instruction: Spend half an hour gardening or tending plants.

name: Sit or stroll in nature for 10-20 minutes
min_effective_dose: >=10 min; most efficient 20-30 min for cortisol (Hunter et al. 2019); a 40-second green view sustained attention in one experiment (not in PubMed)
requirements: outdoors or a window view of greenery
instruction: Sit or stroll somewhere with trees or greenery for ten to twenty minutes. If you cannot get outside, look out at something green.

name: Get outside into daylight
instruction: Step outside into daylight for a while. Evidence is observational (more daily hours outdoors go with less low mood and tiredness). Use sun protection.

name: Splash cold water on your face
min_effective_dose: Cold stimulus to the face during a stressor (28 adults; physiological outcomes only)
instruction: Splash cold water on your face or hold a cool cloth to it for a few moments. Skip this if you have a heart condition.
contraindicated_for: condition:heart_condition=Avoid with heart conditions (general guidance in notes)

name: Cold-water immersion
instruction: Not suggested: an RCT meta-analysis found no immediate stress or mood effect, and cold immersion carries cardiac caution.
contraindicated_for: condition:heart_condition=Cardiac caution;;context:quick_mood_lift_needed=No effect immediately or at 1 h (Cain et al. 2025)

name: Take a short nap (set an alarm)
min_effective_dose: 10 min of sleep (Brooks & Lack 2006, n = 24, sleep-restricted); 5 min gave few benefits; 30 min caused sleep inertia
instruction: Set an alarm and nap for about ten minutes, ideally early afternoon. Longer naps can leave you groggy.
contraindicated_for: context:late_day=Late naps may affect night sleep (general guidance)

name: Coffee then a short nap
min_effective_dose: 200 mg caffeine + <15 min nap in a 30-min break (12 sleepy drivers)
instruction: Drink a coffee, then immediately rest for under fifteen minutes with an alarm set. Tested only in a tiny driving-simulator study.
contraindicated_for: anxious=Avoid caffeine for anxious users;;stressed=Stimulant;;context:late_day=Avoid late afternoon or evening;;condition:caffeine_sensitive=Caffeine

name: Slow paced breathing
min_effective_dose: One 20-min audio session raised relaxation (Toussaint et al. 2021); HRV rises during and right after one session (Laborde et al. 2022)
instruction: Breathe slowly and gently, at roughly six breaths a minute, for five minutes or more. Do not hold your breath for long or breathe fast.

name: Cyclic sighing (long exhale)
min_effective_dose: 5 min/day for 28 days (single trial)
instruction: Inhale through the nose, top up with a second short inhale, then exhale slowly through the mouth. Repeat for five minutes.

name: Box breathing
min_effective_dose: 5 min/day for 28 days (one trial arm; not superior to mindfulness)
instruction: Breathe in, hold, breathe out and hold again for an equal, comfortable count. Repeat for five minutes; keep the holds short.

name: Progressive muscle relaxation
min_effective_dose: One 20-min audio session (60 undergraduates)
instruction: Working from feet to face, tense each muscle group for a few seconds and then release it, for about twenty minutes.

name: Guided imagery
min_effective_dose: One 20-min audio session (60 undergraduates)
instruction: Close your eyes and imagine a calm, pleasant place in detail for about twenty minutes, ideally following an audio guide.

name: Take a time-out and count to ten
instruction: Step away from the situation and count slowly to ten before you respond. This is inferred from calming-activity evidence, not tested on its own.

name: Venting, hitting things or 'blowing off steam'
instruction: Never suggested: venting and arousal-raising activities do not reduce anger and can increase it.
contraindicated_for: angry=g = -0.02 for arousal-increasing activities (Kjaervik & Bushman 2024); hitting a bag while ruminating raised anger (Bushman 2002; not in PubMed);;stressed=Venting;;sad=Venting

name: Mindfulness meditation
min_effective_dose: Single session to ~2 weeks gave g = 0.21 on negative affect (0.04 after bias correction)
instruction: Sit comfortably and rest your attention on your breathing for ten minutes, gently returning to it whenever your mind wanders. Stop if it makes you feel worse.
contraindicated_for: condition:meditation_adverse_reaction=Meditation produces transient adverse effects in a minority (notes Q4)

name: Body scan
instruction: Lie or sit still and slowly move your attention through your body from toes to head. Stop if focusing on the body makes you more uneasy.
contraindicated_for: condition:meditation_adverse_reaction=Body focus can raise distress in some

name: Loving-kindness meditation
min_effective_dose: Single session to weeks (immediate effect not significant vs neutral visualisation)
instruction: Silently wish yourself and then other people well ('may you be happy, may you be safe') for about ten minutes.

name: Self-compassion exercise
instruction: Write or say to yourself what you would say to a good friend in the same situation. Evidence is mostly from multi-session programmes.

name: Write a short gratitude list
instruction: Write down three to five things you are grateful for today. Effects are small and no better than other positive activities.

name: Send a thank-you message
min_effective_dose: One gratitude letter (8-10 min writing)
instruction: Write a short message thanking someone for something specific and send it. People usually underestimate how good it feels to receive.

name: Savour a good moment
instruction: Pause on something good that is happening or happened today: notice the details, tell someone, or let yourself show it.

name: Revisit a happy memory
min_effective_dose: Brief recall task (nostalgia); 10 min twice daily for a week (reminiscence)
instruction: Spend ten minutes recalling a cherished time with people you care about, with old photos or music if you like. Focus on the connection, what it says about the people in your life, rather than on what is gone.

name: Positive psychology exercises (general)
instruction: Reference only: pooled evidence across positive psychology exercises.

name: Look at the situation another way
min_effective_dose: Single instructed use (lab)
instruction: Ask yourself: what is another way to read this situation, and what might I think about it in a month? Best when feelings are mild to moderate.
contraindicated_for: context:high_intensity=Reappraisal is a poor first choice at high emotional intensity (Sheppes et al. 2011)

name: Take a step back (self-distancing)
min_effective_dose: Single instructed use (lab)
instruction: Picture the situation as if you were watching it happen to someone else, or as a fly on the wall, and describe what you see.
contraindicated_for: context:high_intensity=Cognitive strategies are offered after attention-based ones at high intensity

name: Talk to yourself by name
min_effective_dose: Seconds to 3 min (durations not stated in abstracts)
instruction: Silently coach yourself using your own name or 'you' instead of 'I' ('Sam, you have handled this before').

name: Name the feeling
min_effective_dose: Seconds per label (lab/neural evidence)
instruction: Put a precise word on what you feel right now (for example 'tense' or 'disappointed'). If two feelings are present, name both.

name: Do an absorbing task for a few minutes
min_effective_dose: Single use (lab)
requirements: puzzle, game or task of your choice
instruction: Do something that fully occupies your attention for ten minutes: a puzzle, a game or a hands-on task unrelated to what is bothering you.

name: Play a challenge-matched game (e.g. Tetris)
min_effective_dose: Adaptive Tetris session (about 10 min; not confirmed in abstract)
instruction: Play a game such as Tetris at a level that is neither too easy nor too hard, for about ten minutes. Set a timer.

name: Play a casual video game
min_effective_dose: Single short sessions (about 20 min; not confirmed)
instruction: Play a casual game for up to twenty minutes, then stop. Set a timer so it does not crowd out other things.

name: Play a board game with someone
instruction: Play a board or card game with someone. There is little direct evidence for mood or boredom.

name: Sitting alone dwelling on the feeling
instruction: Never suggested: concentrating on the feeling made negative emotion worse, and many people find sitting alone with their thoughts aversive.
contraindicated_for: bored=Many find it aversive (Wilson et al. 2014);;sad=d+ = -0.26 for concentrating on feelings (Webb et al. 2012);;anxious=Same;;angry=Same;;stressed=Same

name: Postpone worry to a set time
min_effective_dose: One 30-min window/day for about a week (not in PubMed)
instruction: Note the worry down and tell yourself you will think it through later, in one fixed 30-minute slot today.

name: Write a specific to-do list or plan
min_effective_dose: 5 min writing (Scullin et al. 2018, n = 57; outcome was sleep onset)
instruction: Spend five minutes writing down everything unfinished, then note when and how you will do each item. You do not need to do them now.

name: Make an if-then plan for the first step
min_effective_dose: One-off plan formation (outcome is goal attainment, not emotion)
instruction: Pick the smallest first step and write it as 'If it is [time/place], then I will [action]'.

name: Do one small pleasant or meaningful activity
instruction: Choose one small thing you usually enjoy or that matters to you, schedule it, and do it for five to ten minutes even if you do not feel like it.

name: Take a micro-break
min_effective_dose: <=10 min (Albulescu et al. 2022)
instruction: Step away from what you are doing for up to ten minutes: stand, stretch, look out of the window or simply rest.

name: Laughter exercises
instruction: Try a laughter-yoga style session with others or a video. Evidence is from multi-session programmes at high risk of bias.

name: Watch something funny
min_effective_dose: Single session of about 9-60 min
instruction: Watch a comedy clip or show that reliably makes you laugh.

name: Take a warm bath or shower
min_effective_dose: 10+ min at 40-42.5 C, 1-2 h before bed (sleep-onset evidence)
instruction: Take a warm bath or shower for ten minutes or more. The evidence is for falling asleep faster when done one to two hours before bed.

name: Smell lavender
min_effective_dose: Often a single exposure (many medical settings; high heterogeneity)
instruction: If you like the scent and have no allergy, inhale lavender oil from a tissue or diffuser for a few minutes.
contraindicated_for: condition:allergy=Allergies

name: L-theanine supplement
instruction: Reference only: the app should not suggest supplements. The evidence does not validate tea drinking.

name: 5-4-3-2-1 grounding
instruction: Name five things you can see, four you can touch, three you can hear, two you can smell and one you can taste. This is practice-based, not evidence-based.

name: Call someone instead of texting
min_effective_dose: Single conversation
instruction: Call or video-call a friend or family member for a few minutes. It usually feels less awkward than people expect; a text is fine if a call feels like too much.
contraindicated_for: condition:social_anxiety=Offer the text fallback

name: Send a 'thinking of you' message
min_effective_dose: Single message (outcome is recipient appreciation)
instruction: Send a short, unexpected message to someone you have not spoken to for a while. People appreciate it more than senders expect.

name: Have a brief friendly chat
min_effective_dose: About 1 minute interaction (single field experiment; not in PubMed)
instruction: Exchange a few genuine words with a barista, neighbour, classmate or colleague.
contraindicated_for: condition:social_anxiety=May be aversive for socially anxious users; context and safety matter

name: Question a negative social assumption
instruction: Notice one negative assumption about how others see you ('they would not want to hear from me') and write down the evidence for and against it. Evidence is for multi-session programmes.

name: Structured loneliness programme
instruction: Reference only: pooled evidence across structured loneliness interventions.

name: Passive social media scrolling
instruction: Never suggested: passive scrolling lowered affective wellbeing through envy.
contraindicated_for: lonely=Passive use lowered affective wellbeing (Verduyn et al. 2015);;sad=Same;;bored=Listed to avoid in the boredom rule (R08);;stressed=Listed to avoid in R04

name: Cap social media at about 30 minutes today
min_effective_dose: About 30 min/day for 3 weeks (single student sample; not in PubMed)
instruction: Set a 30-minute daily limit on social media apps. Tested over three weeks in one student sample.

name: Learn or try something slightly challenging
instruction: Pick something that interests you and is a little challenging but doable: a new skill, a small project, a lesson. Boredom usually means the current activity is too easy, too hard or not meaningful.
contraindicated_for: tired=Demanding challenge is avoided when tired (R07, R20)

name: Do something entirely of your own choosing
instruction: Reference only: having control over off-job time is associated with vigour (correlational). Supports letting the user pick.

name: Drink a glass of water
instruction: Drink a glass of water if you have not had much today. Evidence is only that dehydration impairs thinking, not that extra water energises.

name: Tidy one small area
instruction: Clear one small surface or corner for ten minutes. There is no intervention evidence; skip it if it feels like one more chore.

name: Do a small act of kindness
min_effective_dose: Varied (single act to weeks)
instruction: Do one small kind thing for someone today: help, a compliment, a favour.

name: Spend a little on someone else
min_effective_dose: One purchase for someone else
requirements: another person; a small amount of money
instruction: If money is not tight, buy a small treat or gift for someone else.
contraindicated_for: condition:financial_stress=Do not push spending on users in financial stress

name: Plan to volunteer
instruction: Look for a volunteering opportunity for the coming weeks. This is a plan-ahead suggestion, not a 5-30 minute activity.
contraindicated_for: context:quick_mood_lift_needed=Sustained activity; trials inconclusive for mood

name: Share good news with someone
min_effective_dose: Single disclosures
instruction: Tell someone who is likely to be pleased for you about something good that happened.

name: Fault-finding or suppressing a good moment
instruction: Never suggested: dampening strategies go with lower positive affect.
contraindicated_for: content=Associated with lower positive affect (Quoidbach et al. 2010; not in PubMed);;calm=Same;;energetic=Same

name: Use a good mood to explore or learn
instruction: While you feel good, try something new, learn something or reach out to someone.

name: Share a hug or affectionate touch
min_effective_dose: Adult sessions median 20 min (mostly massage-type interventions)
requirements: a willing partner, friend or family member
instruction: Ask someone close to you for a hug, or hold hands for a while. Only with their clear consent.
contraindicated_for: context:no_willing_partner=Not for users without a willing partner; consent essential

name: Pet a dog or cat
min_effective_dose: 10 min hands-on (not in PubMed)
instruction: Spend ten minutes stroking a friendly dog or cat.
contraindicated_for: condition:allergy=Allergies or fear of animals

name: Reframe the jitters as excitement
min_effective_dose: One sentence of self-talk ('I am excited') before a performance task (Brooks 2014); pooled performance d = 0.23 (Bosshard & Gomez 2024)
instruction: If something is coming up, say out loud 'I am excited' and treat the racing heart as energy that will help you. In experiments this worked better than trying to calm down; slow breathing is a fine alternative.
contraindicated_for: context:no_upcoming_task=Tested on anxiety before a performance or exam; without a task, calming options remain reasonable (mixed_state_interventions.md section 6)

name: Write about it from a distance
min_effective_dose: Single session of self-distanced reflection (Kross et al. 2005; Kross et al. 2012); tested as reflection, not as writing
instruction: Once you have calmed down a little, write a few lines about what happened as if describing someone else: use your name or 'you', and ask why they felt that way instead of replaying the scene.
contraindicated_for: context:high_intensity=Calm down or distract first; rumination after provocation increased aggression (Bushman et al. 2005)

name: Set up regular calls with someone who listens
min_effective_dose: Daily calls for 5 days, then at least twice a week for 4 weeks (Kahlon et al. 2021, n = 240 homebound adults)
instruction: Arrange short, regular phone calls with a warm person who mostly listens and asks about you: a friend, a relative or a telephone befriending service. In the trial, calls were daily for five days, then at least twice a week.

name: Get a pet to feel better
instruction: Not suggested. Owning a pet was not associated with lower depression in a meta-analysis of observational studies, so the app should not suggest getting a pet as a fix.
contraindicated_for: sad=Pet ownership and depression OR 1.03 (n.s.); cat ownership OR 1.06 (Moshfeghinia et al. 2025);;lonely=Do not suggest getting a pet as a fix for loneliness (mixed_state_interventions.md section 4)
